parsed.explanation: The combined regime is actively hostile to trans travellers at the two points where discovery is engineered: the border and gendered facilities. National passport/visa rules (post-January 2025, upheld November 2025) bar self-selected markers, eliminate new X markers, and direct officers to refuse cases with sex doubt and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; allied governments have issued advisories and citizens of a neighbouring jurisdiction were detained over visa issues. The division adds a K-12 facility ban, an extended Act 619 misdemeanour for trans bathroom use with a minor present, a rescinded X licence marker, no state hate-crime or anti-discrimination coverage, and a religious-refusal healthcare law; it sits one tier below 'Do Not Travel'. Mitigating: no criminalisation of trans identity, national hate-crime and Bostock coverage, functioning courts that have enjoined several orders, and legal-aid guidance.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport/visa markers restricted to birth sex; X markers discontinued for new issues; officers instructed to refuse cases where sex is doubted and to weigh material-misrepresentation findings carrying permanent ineligibility; reports of passports blocked/confiscated and travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid to expiry; the fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist; litigation continues and a legal-aid FAQ documents options.
entry_documents.interaction: A traveller whose marker, photograph or presentation mismatch triggers secondary screening, refusal, or a fraud referral that can migrate into immigration detention and birth-sex custody placement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documented as abusive for transgender detainees: forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse; national prisons adopt conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Detention is not automatic; courts have enjoined several executive orders; consular and legal-aid recourse exists in principle.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy -> refusal/pending case -> detention is the documented pathway, and placement/conditions in custody are the harshest feature of the regime.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars federally funded single-sex facility access by identity; division bans trans students from congruent school facilities (2023, extended 2025) and makes trans use of public restrooms/changing rooms with a minor present a misdemeanour where intent to arouse is shown.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Act 619 requires both willful entry and an intent element, not automatic arrest; the division's ban is stated as K-12-scoped, and many categories of public buildings are not documented as covered.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: An adult travelling with a minor faces the sharpest convergence: presence of a child is the statutory trigger, and a complaint can arrive through a member of the public rather than an enforcement officer.

care_services.exposure: Division law lets practitioners cite religious belief to deny LGBT patients care; care ban for minors litigated with enforcement reinstated in August 2025; national measures target youth care funding.
care_services.protection: Care ban was struck down once and remains contested; national insurance rules are proposed, not final.
care_services.interaction: An injured or ill visitor may face refusal at the point of disclosure, with the only recourse being a national civil-rights claim, not a state one.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for prioritised neutralisation; January 2025 orders direct investigation of schools affirming trans minors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The same strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; the reward memorandum never lists gender ideology as a criterion; courts have enjoined several orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Raises the chance that a discovered trans traveller's advocacy, materials or online content is reframed as security-relevant at a checkpoint.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans parent travelling with a child crosses the division's minor-present misdemeanour trigger and school facility bans; national orders contemplate criminal referral of adults who affirm a trans minor.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented protection specific to visiting guardians; national hate-crime coverage does not reach this.
minors_guardians.interaction: Border secondary screening of a family can produce separation questions and referral of the adult, which is not documented as mitigated anywhere in the dossier.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division has no hate-crime enhancement and its civil intimidation remedy excludes gender identity; local protections are unenforced under the 2015 pre-emption act.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute has covered gender identity since 2009 and applies in the division.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A visitor assaulted locally relies on national rather than local recourse, and the documented enforcement gap sits with the state, not the national authority.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Whether Act 619 has produced any arrests is undocumented; whether the division's facility ban reaches adult public buildings beyond the minor-present clause is unstated; the care ban's operative status is unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation, injunctions, a documented legal-aid FAQ and functioning courts give real, if partial, remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Enforcement of the harshest rules is efficient where enacted, so 'the courts work' cuts against the traveller on the passport and facility rules rather than for them.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor shows arbitrary, extorting officials with no institutional protection and a coerced statement following the traveller. This jurisdiction is clearly above it: statutory limits, a documented legal-aid FAQ, an independent judiciary that has enjoined several orders, and national hate-crime coverage. The abuse here is policy-driven, not unofficial predation.

That anchor denies entry after invasive review but grants an explicit bar on detention, so no custody follows. This jurisdiction is materially below it: custody and its documented harms (forced labour, sexual abuse, hormone removal) are a live step on the pathway, facility restrictions are state-imposed, and the division adds a misdemeanour, even though no trans-specific offence exists as such.

That anchor's encounter ends with a supervisor invoking published guidelines and issuing a permit. No equivalent functioning safeguard is documented here for the traveller: the guidelines themselves direct refusal and contemplate permanent ineligibility, and court relief has been partial and contested.

That anchor has a privacy directive working on request plus an institutional apology. Here the operative federal rules do the opposite of protecting the traveller, so a remedy of that order is unavailable.

parsed.synthesis: Discovery is the engineered risk here: passport and visa processing now assumes birth-sex markers, officers are cued to doubt sex and to weigh lifetime fraud findings, and the division supplies its own facility ban plus a minor-present misdemeanour. If discovery escalates into immigration custody, the documented conditions are severe (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse, hormone removal in custody). Against that, trans identity is not criminalised, national hate-crime and employment protections exist, no sodomy statute operates, courts have blocked several orders, and legal aid publishes practical guidance. The result sits between the arbitrary-predation tier and the clean-administrative-exclusion tier, held down by state-perpetrated exposures rather than street-level hostility.
